subject: science
domain: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

items.prompt:
Newton's second law is written as
A) F = ma
B) F = m + a
C) a = F + m
D) m = Fa

steps: Net force equals mass times acceleration.

items.prompt:
A net force of 10 N on a 2 kg cart gives an acceleration of
A) 5 m/s squared
B) 20 m/s squared
C) 12 m/s squared
D) 2 m/s squared

For the same force, more mass gives ____ acceleration.
A) less
B) more
C) the same
D) no

steps: More mass means less acceleration for the same force.

items.prompt:
A 4 kg object accelerates at 3 m/s squared. The net force is
A) 12 N
B) 7 N
C) 1.3 N
D) 1 N

A 3 kg object has a net force of 9 N. Its acceleration is
A) 3 m/s squared
B) 27 m/s squared
C) 6 m/s squared
D) 12 m/s squared

A 2 kg ball and a 6 kg ball each get 12 N. Which accelerates more?
A) The 2 kg ball
B) The 6 kg ball
C) They are equal
D) Neither accelerates

steps: Less mass means more acceleration: 6 vs 2.

items.prompt:
Data show acceleration doubles when force doubles at constant mass. This supports
A) F = ma
B) that mass has no effect
C) that force has no effect
D) nothing

steps: Proportional force and acceleration support F = ma.
